## Viña del Mar and Valparaiso in one sightseeing day

From [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), we set out for two coastal cities. Viña del Mar reveals itself through its amphitheatre and avenues made for strolling, while Valparaiso offers a square near the port, a historic hillside lift and a panoramic terrace. The group excursion takes a full day, returning to Santiago afterwards.

## Viña del Mar: Quinta Vergara and the coastal avenues

The first part of the route includes the [Quinta Vergara](/chile/place/quinta-vergara-amphitheater/) amphitheatre. It is best known as the venue of the Viña del Mar International Song Festival. Our sightseeing day is devoted to discovering the city and its attractions.

We then continue along San Martín Avenue and Peru Avenue. These stops capture the city's coastal atmosphere before we move to Valparaiso's port neighbourhoods. Both cities are covered on one excursion, so there is no need to plan a separate overnight stay on the coast for this programme.

## Valparaiso: Sotomayor, El Peral and Paseo Yugoslavo

In Valparaiso, you will see [Plaza Sotomayor](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/) and then ride the [El Peral funicular](/chile/place/el-peral-funicular/). Its upper station connects with [Paseo Yugoslavo](/chile/place/paseo-yugoslavo/), a promenade terrace overlooking the port. The Russian itinerary also refers to this section as the Yugoslav Corridor.

This sequence lets you experience the city at different levels: first the central square, then the hillside and the port panorama. For general information about both cities, see the [Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) page.

## Format and place within a longer journey

This is a full-day group excursion. We agree on the guide's language, departure time and price for a standalone booking when arranging the trip.

On our [15-day tour of Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), this outing takes place on day ten. The previous day is spent exploring Santiago, and after visiting the coast you return to the same city for the night. The next day, the itinerary continues with a flight to Peru. Excursions and admission tickets specified in the tour are included in the package; domestic flights are paid for separately.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which city does the excursion depart from?

We depart from Santiago de Chile and return there after the excursion. Valparaiso and Viña del Mar are covered in one sightseeing day.

### Which funicular is included?

We ride El Peral and then walk along Paseo Yugoslavo. This is the exact itinerary of this excursion and is worth noting when comparing Valparaiso trips.

### Can this excursion be part of a multi-day tour?

Yes. It is included in our [15-day journey through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). The full trip's duration, accommodation and price are available on the tour page.

## Tours featuring Quinta Vergara, El Peral and Paseo Yugoslavo

This selection brings together tours featuring our [Viña del Mar and Valparaiso excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-valparaiso-quinta-vergara-el-peral/). Its route includes the [Quinta Vergara](/chile/place/quinta-vergara-amphitheater/) amphitheatre, San Martín and Peru avenues, Plaza Sotomayor, the [El Peral funicular](/chile/place/el-peral-funicular/) and [Paseo Yugoslavo](/chile/place/paseo-yugoslavo/). When choosing a longer trip, consider how this day fits among the flights and other excursions.

## The Chilean coast on a four-country trip

Our [15-day tour of Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) starts in Rio de Janeiro, then visits both sides of Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires. You arrive in Santiago on day nine and discover the historic and modern sides of the capital.

The following day, we head towards the Pacific Ocean. Viña del Mar and Valparaiso offer a different kind of city walk: seaside avenues, a port, an ascent up the hillside and views from a terrace. The itinerary returns to Santiago in the evening, and day eleven begins with onward travel to Cusco and the Sacred Valley of the Incas.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru}}

## What a separate day on the coast means

The Chilean part of the tour includes two nights in Santiago. The trip to [Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) therefore takes place without changing hotels to another city. The coastal day is followed by the Peruvian part of the journey, including the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Cusco and Lima.

When choosing this option, bear in mind the pace of the whole tour: four countries are covered in 15 days and 14 nights. An extended seaside holiday would require additional time; in this programme, Chile's coast is explored on an excursion from the capital.

## How to read the tour price

The package includes accommodation with breakfast, transfers, excursions along the route, admission tickets and the Vistadome train to Machu Picchu. Domestic and international flights are paid for separately. Compare the full cost of the journey including airfare, even if another tour follows a similar sequence of countries.

Prices, duration, accommodation options and the tariff year are shown on the tour page.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do you need to stay overnight in Valparaiso?

On the described 15-day programme, we return to Santiago after the excursion, with an overnight stay there.

### When does the Peruvian section begin?

After two nights in Santiago: on day eleven, you fly to Cusco and continue to the Sacred Valley. Lima comes at the end of the Peruvian route.

### Is this a group excursion?

Yes. The outing to Viña del Mar and Valparaiso is designated as a full-day group excursion in this programme.

## Excursions from Santiago to VIK Winery

[VIK Winery](/chile/place/vik-winery/) is located in Millahue Valley, in the Cachapoal wine region. Its hills, vineyards and distinctive production-complex architecture show how winemaking relates to the surrounding landscape. Travellers discover wine production and taste wines from the estate.

We offer **two excursions**. One is a full-day journey by road; the other includes round-trip helicopter flights from Santiago, a private tasting and lunch. These are different travel products, and the included services depend on the excursion selected.

## Comparing the itineraries

| Format | Confirmed programme |
|---|---|
| [Tasting and lunch from Santiago](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-tasting-lunch-from-santiago/) | Full day, overland trip, winery visit, tasting and restaurant |
| [Helicopter and private tasting](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-helicopter-tasting-lunch/) | Return flights, winery tour, private tasting and lunch |

For the [VIK excursion by road](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-tasting-lunch-from-santiago/), the drive from Santiago takes approximately **2 hours**. On arrival, guests learn about the winery's production, taste estate wines and enjoy lunch overlooking the valley. The trip takes a full day.

In the [helicopter option](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-helicopter-tasting-lunch/), the flight takes **around 40 minutes each way**. Following the aerial transfer, the programme includes an introduction to VIK, a guided winery visit, a private tasting and lunch. The flight above central Chile is thus an important part of the experience in its own right.

## What is interesting about VIK beyond wine tasting?

The winery is known for its contemporary architecture and its work with grapes grown in Millahue Valley. A visit offers an opportunity to explore the vineyards, learn how wine is made and compare different wines.

The VIK complex also has hotel and restaurant facilities. **Booking an excursion does not include an overnight hotel stay or access to all of the estate's separate activities.** The precise wines, menu, presentation of dishes and tasting times depend on the arrangements agreed for your trip.

## How to choose an excursion

If you want to devote a day to the winery and lunch without flying, choose the overland excursion. The helicopter option is designed for travellers who prioritise a private format and aerial views of the valley.

Agree on the number of participants, dietary requirements and tasting arrangements for your travel date. The aerial option additionally depends on the weather and confirmation of the helicopter transfer. No separate guaranteed price is provided on the public tour pages, so compare costs based on the actual quotations for each option.

For other wine destinations, explore our [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [food and wine trips](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Frequently asked questions about VIK Winery

### How long does it take to get to VIK from Santiago?

For the overland excursion, allow **around 2 hours** by road. The helicopter flight takes approximately **40 minutes one way**.

### Is lunch included in both excursions?

Yes, lunch is mentioned in the descriptions of both options. The specific dishes and wines have not been separately stipulated in the public text.

### Is the tasting private in both options?

A private format is expressly specified for the [helicopter excursion](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-helicopter-tasting-lunch/). A tasting is confirmed for the regular overland trip, but not a separate exclusive event.

### Is overnight accommodation at VIK included?

No. An overnight stay is not included in either of the two one-day products described.

## VIK Winery: helicopter flight from Santiago, tasting and lunch

[VIK Winery](/chile/place/vik-winery/) is situated in Millahue Valley in central Chile, among vineyards and hills. We offer this experience in a special format: **return helicopter flights from Santiago**, a personalised introduction to the winery, a private tasting and lunch.

The one-way flight takes about **40 minutes**. From the air, you can see agricultural valleys and the Andean foothills. The journey itself becomes an experience before you have even started learning about the wines.

## Helicopter transfer: from the capital to the vineyards

The trip begins in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). As the helicopter leaves the city, the urban scenery gives way to fields, hills and vineyards. Flying offers another perspective on central Chile's terrain and the location of its wineries.

The itinerary includes an equivalent return flight to Santiago. Whether the flight can operate depends on weather, aviation regulations and the agreed trip arrangements. The exact departure location, baggage limitations and number of passengers are confirmed for each booking.

**About 40 minutes each way** is the flight time specified in the programme, not the duration of the entire excursion.

## Millahue Valley and what makes VIK distinctive

[Millahue Valley](/chile/place/millahue-valley/) is located in the Cachapoal area. Vineyards share the landscape with natural hills, and the relief, soils and climatic variations influence the approach to winemaking.

VIK is known for bringing together winemaking technology, a terroir-focused approach and modern architecture. The cellar building designed by architect Smiljan Radić is an attraction in itself: it is integrated into the surrounding landscape, and its design highlights the connection between art and production.

During the estate tour, visitors can learn about VIK's approach to vineyards, winemaking and ageing. A winery visit is included, but the programme does not specify access to every production room or a separate masterclass with the winemaker.

## Private wine tasting and lunch

The winery visit is followed by a **private tasting of VIK wines**. This provides a relaxed setting for appreciating the wines' aromas, structure and differences with the participants in your party. The exact list of labels and vintages depends on the confirmed itinerary; it must not be substituted with wines from other VIK tasting packages.

**Lunch** follows. The precise menu and wine pairings are agreed for this trip. VIK's official website describes restaurants and separate culinary programmes, but this does not mean that any of those packages are automatically included in the Ada Tours helicopter excursion.

All elements matter together in this product: the aerial journey, introduction to the winery, private tasting and lunch. It is a standalone premium experience, distinct from a short cellar tour with an ordinary road transfer.

## Who is this winery day for?

Travellers choose this format for a special occasion, a trip for two, a private group or a holiday where they want to devote a day to wine and food. Discuss tasting preferences, dietary restrictions and whether particular guests can participate ahead of time.

Alcohol tasting is intended for adults in accordance with local law. Travellers who do not drink wine should confirm with the organiser whether alternative drinks are available.

There is **no separate published price** for this trip. The cost is calculated for the specific itinerary; the price of an ordinary VIK tasting must not be used as the helicopter package price.

## Fitting VIK into a trip through Chile

Departing from and returning to Santiago makes it possible to devote a separate part of a wider journey through central Chile to the winery. For other wine regions, the [Food and Wine](/interests/food-and-wine/) thematic catalogue is a useful starting point. For a broader itinerary, see our [Chile tours](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about VIK

### How do you reach the winery?

Under the Ada Tours programme, you fly by helicopter from Santiago and back. Each one-way flight takes around 40 minutes.

### What does the day at VIK include?

A winery visit, private tasting, lunch and return helicopter transfers.

### Can you request an ordinary car transfer instead of a helicopter?

The published product specifically uses a helicopter. Alternative logistics can be discussed as a separate programme, rather than automatically describing it as the same package.

### How much does the excursion cost?

No separate sum has been fixed. The quotation depends on the travellers and the confirmed arrangements for the selected trip.

## VIK Winery from Santiago: excursion, wine tasting and lunch

[VIK Winery](/chile/place/vik-winery/) is located in [Millahue Valley](/chile/place/millahue-valley/) in Chile's Cachapoal region. Vineyards cover the hillsides, while the winery's contemporary architecture stands out against the rural surroundings. The visit introduces both wine production and the landscape where its grapes are grown.

We offer a **full-day excursion from Santiago**. The drive to the winery takes **approximately 2 hours**. After breakfast at the hotel, travellers head towards Cachapoal to visit the production facilities, taste VIK wines and have lunch in a restaurant overlooking the valley.

## What the winery visit includes

The central part of the experience is a guided winery visit explaining how the wines are made. Participants learn about the production process, from growing and handling grapes to ageing and preparing the finished wines. Exactly which technical areas are open to visitors depends on the winery's current route.

This is followed by a **tasting of premium VIK wines**. The number of wines, grape varieties, vintages and any special tasting formats are confirmed for the chosen date.

The programme concludes with **lunch at a restaurant overlooking the vineyards**. This is a separate part of the visit, allowing more time in Millahue Valley. The exact menu and any wine pairings also need to be agreed with the organiser.

## Why Millahue Valley appeals to wine lovers

[Millahue](/chile/place/millahue-valley/) is a rural valley in central Chile, where vineyards stand beside hills and natural landscapes. A winery visit offers more than a chance to taste individual wines: it is also an opportunity to understand the conditions in which grapes are grown.

VIK's architecture has become a striking part of the estate's identity. The building is integrated into the surrounding hills and feels like an extension of the vineyard scenery. The visit allows guests to appreciate both the natural foundations of winemaking and contemporary approaches to wine production.

If you are planning a journey around culinary experiences, the [Food and Wine selection](/interests/food-and-wine/) brings together other current options in this category.

## How to plan a full day from Santiago

Allow approximately 2 hours on the road **in each direction**, as well as time for the winery tour, tasting and lunch. It is therefore best not to fill the evening in Santiago with tightly scheduled activities.

The excursion departs after breakfast and takes a full day. However, **the precise transfer time, vehicle type, guide language, fixed price and list of included charges are not specified**. Even though tasting and lunch are part of the itinerary, their commercial terms should be confirmed for the chosen offer.

Alcohol tasting is for adults and subject to local regulations. Travellers who do not consume alcohol should ask in advance about non-alcoholic alternatives and participation arrangements; these have not yet been specified.

## How this differs from a short wine tasting

A brief visit to a wine bar focuses mainly on sampling drinks. The VIK excursion includes a trip from the capital to the wine region, an introduction to production, a tasting and a restaurant lunch. It offers a more substantial experience, but also requires more time.

Other outings are available in the [Chile excursions catalogue](/chile/excursion/), while the estate's geography is explained in more detail on the [VIK page](/chile/place/vik-winery/).

## Frequently asked questions about VIK Winery

### How long is the journey from Santiago?

The Ada Tours itinerary specifies **approximately 2 hours** from Santiago to Millahue Valley. Actual travel time depends on the departure point and road conditions.

### Is wine tasting part of the programme?

Yes, **a tasting of premium VIK wines** is named as part of the excursion. The number of wines and commercial terms need to be confirmed for your chosen option.

### Is lunch provided?

Yes, lunch is described at a restaurant overlooking the valley and vineyards. The menu and drinks should be agreed separately.

### How much does the trip cost?

No fixed price is published on the current page. The cost is calculated for the actual programme and number of participants.
